warnings: ⚠️ MISFILED AT THE AGENCY, AND SHELVED WITH ITS SOURCE ANYWAY. This document's subject is the MANSFIELD WWTP in RICHLAND County — not Lima, and not Allen County. Its own Ohio EPA reference block reads "Re: Mansfield WWTP / Correspondence / NPDES / Richland County / 2PE00000", pairing Mansfield's plant and county with LIMA's permit number. That is why a portal sweep of permit 2PE00000 returned it, and why it sits in data/documents/oepa/lima/.

The extraction is shelved under oepa/lima/ because the extracted tree MIRRORS its source and the source is immutable — the byte was served under Lima's permit and keeps that identity. Nothing here is Lima evidence: `respondent`, `facility` and every figure describe Mansfield. Read the shelf as custody, not as attribution.

RE-ATTRIBUTED AT THE READ LAYER, NOT MOVED (#2085). data/corpus-attribution.yaml — a reviewed, document-cited overlay — declares this artifact `attributed_to: mansfield`, and `watermark.sites.effective_corpus_scope` folds that into the scope as an exact-relpath grant. The document therefore leaves Lima's cross-document layer (timeline, entities, the records/documents feeds, retrieval, the agent read tools) and joins Mansfield's, which is a registered site with its own committed record under oepa/mansfield/. Its BYTES do not move and this file does not move: the shelf still records what Ohio EPA served, and the overlay records what the document is about.

`permit_no: 2PE00000` is AS PRINTED and is the error itself, not a transcription of Mansfield's real permit. Do not 'correct' it to a Mansfield permit number — the printed value is the evidence that the misfiling happened. Mansfield's actual NPDES id is not stated in this document.
Permit number '2PE00000' may be a placeholder or file-reference identifier rather than the full active NPDES permit number; verify against permit records.

fields.respondent: City of Mansfield (Mr. Robert Coker Jr., WWTP Manager)

obligations.requirement: PMP report must be prepared for all pollutants other than hexavalent chromium and bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (which Ohio EPA agrees may be excluded) and submitted annually as required by NPDES permit Part I, C-A.3.

fields.summary: Ohio EPA responds to the Mansfield WWTP's February 24, 2020 letter regarding the Pollutants Control Strategy required under NPDES permit Part I, C-A.2. Ohio EPA concurs with the WWTP's request to exclude hexavalent chromium and bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate from the Pollutant Minimization Program (PMP) report requirements, given five years of non-detect data for those parameters. The City is directed to continue submitting the annual PMP report for all other pollutants per Part I, C-A.3.
fields.note: Ohio EPA's response to the City of Mansfield's 2020-02-24 submittal of the pollutant Control Strategy required by its NPDES permit Part I, C-A.2 — covering copper, dissolved hexavalent chromium and bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate. Mansfield is a registered site in this network (the first documented data-center rejection site), so this is a document Mansfield's own record should know about; it is reachable only because Ohio EPA filed it under Lima's permit number. Acted on in #2085, at the read layer: the attribution overlay routes this artifact into Mansfield's corpus scope while its bytes stay here, because moving or re-shelving the source byte is exactly what the chain-of-custody rule forbids.

title: Mansfield Wastewater Treatment Plant
warnings: THE RECEIVING WATER IS BLANK ON THE FACE OF THE PERMIT. The authorization sentence on sheet 1 reads "... located at 385 S. Illinois Ave, Mansfield, Ohio, Richland County, to (River Mile 11.18) in accordance with the conditions specified in Parts I, II, III, IV, V, and VI of this permit." The stream name is simply absent between "to" and "(River Mile 11.18)". This was checked against a 300 DPI render of the page, so it is the document's own defect and NOT a text-extraction artifact. The receiving water is recoverable only from Part II Item B's station table (sheet 25), which names it on station 002. Anyone citing the authorization sentence alone will find no water named in it.

THE LIMIT TABLE YOU WANT DEPENDS ON THE DATE, and the difference is narrower than it looks. Part I.A carries THREE tables: one for outfall 001 (whole term), and two for outfall 002 — an "Initial" table for the effective date through the end of the 36th month, and a "Final" table from the 37th month to expiration. Transcribing both and diffing them parameter by parameter, the ONLY substantive change is whole effluent toxicity on FATHEAD MINNOW: acute TUa and chronic TUc go from monitor-only to numerically limited. Every other limit — TP, ammonia, E. coli, total residual chlorine, B2EHP, the metals, mercury, cyanide — is IDENTICAL in both tables, and Ceriodaphnia dubia stays monitor-only throughout. Do not assume the phase-in loosens the conventional pollutants; it does not touch them.

THE PERMIT NAMES TWO DIFFERENT OHIO EPA DISTRICT OFFICES for two schedules at the same facility. Part I.C.A (Toxicity Reduction Evaluation) directs every TRE submittal to the "Northwest District Office" — four times, at items 2, 3 and 4. Part I.C.B (Municipal Pretreatment Schedule) directs its submittal to "Ohio EPA, Central Office Pretreatment Unit and to Ohio EPA, Northeast District Office." Both are transcribed below as printed. Which office actually holds the Mansfield file is `[open]` — no captured source in this corpus establishes Ohio EPA's district assignment for Richland County, and it matters practically: a records request for the TRE submittals has to be addressed to one of them.

THE WET LIMITS AND THE BIOMONITORING PROGRAM NAME DIFFERENT STATIONS. Part I.A puts the toxicity parameters (61425-61428) in the outfall 002 tables — final effluent after blending. Part II Item U (sheet 33) says the permittee "shall continue to implement an effluent biomonitoring program to determine the toxicity of the effluent from outfall 2PE00001001" — secondary effluent BEFORE blending — and repeats 001 for both the chronic and acute bioassays. Item U defers to Part I.A for the test specification ("as specified in Part I,A"), so the station may be a drafting carryover, but the two parts do not agree on their face and this file does not resolve it. It matters: 002 is 001 blended with the equalization-basin bypass (602) and stormwater (603), so the two streams are not the same sample, and a TRE turns on which one is toxic.

sampling_stations.transcription_note: The permit prints "2PE0001602", "2PE0001603" and "2PE0001001" (seven digits, one short) inside the descriptions of stations 001, 602 and 603. The typo is the document's; the station KEYS above use the correct eight-digit form and this note records the source's spelling rather than silently normalizing it away.

effluent_limits_001.period: effective date through expiration — one table, no phase-in
effluent_limits_001.design_flow_basis: "Effluent loadings based on average design flow of 12.0 MGD." (the permit's own note)

ammonia_nh3.note: MONITOR ONLY at 001. The numeric ammonia limits are at 002.

effluent_limits_001.note: 001 carries NO phosphorus, ammonia, toxicity, metals or bacteria limit. It is the technology-based point: solids and oxygen demand only. Every water-quality-based limit at this plant attaches at 002.

effluent_limits_002.citation: Permit 2PE00001*PD, sheets 3-5 (Initial) and 6-8 (Final), Part I.A.2 and I.A.3
effluent_limits_002.design_flow_basis: "Effluent loadings based on average design flow of 12.0 MGD."
effluent_limits_002.initial_period: "During the period beginning on the effective date of this permit and lasting until the end of the 36th month after the effective date" — 2025-07-01 through on or about 2028-06-30.
effluent_limits_002.final_period: "During the period beginning on the 37th month after the effective date of this permit and lasting until the expiration date" — on or about 2028-07-01 through 2030-03-31.
effluent_limits_002.changeover_date_note: The permit never prints a calendar date for the changeover — only "the 36th month" and "the 37th month after the effective date." Resolved against the 2025-07-01 effective date those become 2028-06-30 and 2028-07-01. That arithmetic is [inference]; no captured source (ICIS-NPDES is not committed for this facility) independently carries the interim limit-set end date, so unlike Bowling Green's 2PD00009 there is no second system to agree with here.

unchanged_across_the_phase_in.note: These apply IDENTICALLY in both the Initial and Final tables. Transcribed once.
unchanged_across_the_phase_in.monitor_only_parameters: TKN, nitrite+nitrate, dissolved orthophosphate, total filterable residue, flow rate, and the metals suite (Se, Ni, Zn, Cd, Pb, Cr total, Cu, Cr dissolved hexavalent) plus low-level mercury and free cyanide — all carry monitoring frequencies and NO numeric limit, in both tables.

the_only_change_at_month_37.what: whole effluent toxicity limits on fathead minnow (Pimephales promelas)

ceriodaphnia_dubia.both_tables: MONITOR ONLY in BOTH tables — 2/Year, 24hr Composite, February and August. The water flea gains no limit at any point in this permit term.

the_only_change_at_month_37.also_changed_but_not_a_limit: B2EHP's sampling type is printed "1/Month Composite" in the Initial table and "1/Month 24hr Composite" in the Final table. Same numeric limits. Recorded for completeness so a future diff of these two tables does not read it as a substantive change.

sso_300.note: The permit is explicit that the 1/Month frequency is a REPORTING frequency, not a monitoring one: "these overflows shall be monitored on each day when they discharge." Only SSOs that reach waters of the state — directly or through a storm sewer — are reported at this station. Each location overflowing on a given day counts as one occurrence, so a two-location day is two.
sso_300.annual_report: An annual SSO report covering ALL overflows in the collection system (including those that never reach waters of the state) is due March 31 for the prior calendar year, with SSO locations numbered consecutively from 301, volumes in millions of gallons, and a narrative analysis of water-in-basement patterns by location, frequency and cause.

biosolids_581.also_monitored: ammonia, total Kjeldahl nitrogen, total phosphorus, potassium (nutrient suite, no limits)

sludge_586.applies_to: disposal in a municipal solid waste landfill

sludge_588.applies_to: transfer to another NPDES permit holder

influent_601.description: Influent monitoring downstream of the bar screen — all monitor-only, no limits
influent_601.parameters: TSS, total cyanide, nickel, zinc, cadmium, lead, total chromium, copper, dissolved hexavalent chromium, B2EHP, low-level mercury, pH minimum, CBOD 5-day.
influent_601.note: "Samples of influent used for determination of net values or percent removal must be taken the same day as those samples of effluent used for that determination", and sampling for common parameters occurs the same day as outfall 001.

bypass_602.description: Bypass from the equalization basin — monitored WHEN DISCHARGING, and it carries real limits
bypass_602.note: A DMR for this station must be submitted EVERY month whether or not it discharged, and monitoring is reported on each day there is a discharge. Occurrence, volume and duration may be estimated if no measuring device is available.

stormwater_603.note: Stormwater — see Parts IV, V and VI (the SWPPP parts).

upstream_801.chemistry: ammonia, total Kjeldahl nitrogen, nitrite+nitrate, total phosphorus — 1/Month Grab, all months
upstream_801.bacteria: E. coli, 1 per 2 Weeks Grab, June - Aug
upstream_801.ambient_toxicity: 48-hr acute Ceriodaphnia dubia (61432) and 7-day chronic Ceriodaphnia dubia (61438), 2/Year Grab, February and August; 96-hr acute Pimephales promelas (61435) and 7-day chronic Pimephales promelas (61441), 1/Quarter Grab, Quarterly - Tox2. Reported as "% Affected", no limits.
upstream_801.significance: The upstream station runs the SAME toxicity battery as the effluent. That is what makes a Toxicity Reduction Evaluation answerable — it separates plant-caused toxicity from what Rocky Fork already carries past the plant. Note the asymmetry with Part I.A: the ambient tests here run on BOTH species at full frequency, while only the fathead minnow gains a numeric limit at the outfall.

downstream_farfield_901.description: Receiving stream BELOW the discharge, at the State Route 39 bridge
downstream_farfield_901.parameters: Water temperature, pH, ammonia, total Kjeldahl nitrogen, nitrite+nitrate, total phosphorus, total hardness (as CaCO3) — 1/Month Grab, all months; E. coli 1 per 2 Weeks Grab, June - Aug.
downstream_farfield_901.note: Sampling for the respective/common parameters shall occur on the same day as Outfall 2PE00001001.
downstream_farfield_901.significance: 801 + 901 together are a committed monthly upstream/downstream nutrient record on Rocky Fork, arriving through DMRs for the life of the permit (to 2030-03-31). It is an ambient dataset the city is obliged to produce, not one anybody has to go collect.

event_code_forms.note: ⚠️ THE PERMIT PRINTS ITS OWN EVENT CODES TWO DIFFERENT WAYS, and the blocks below preserve whichever form appears where each is transcribed rather than harmonizing them. The milestone table on sheet 21 prints them UNPADDED; the narrative sections print them ZERO-PADDED to five digits. So a code differing between `milestone_summary_report` and the narrative blocks is the DOCUMENT disagreeing with itself, not a transcription error.
event_code_forms.no_narrative_code_for_the_interim_report: TRE step 2 (the 2026-04-01 interim report) is the one milestone the narrative gives NO event code at all — steps 3 and 4 end "(Event Code 34599)" and "(Event Code 05699)", and step 2 simply does not. The table's `7099` is the only code for that milestone anywhere in this permit. A records request citing an event code for the interim report should use `7099` and expect the agency's system may hold it padded.

milestone_summary_report.note: Transcribed verbatim from the permit's own table, INCLUDING its unpadded event codes — see event_code_forms above before diffing these against the narrative blocks. The dates are CALENDAR dates the permit prints — not offsets, and not inferred.

toxicity_reduction_evaluation.preamble: "As soon as possible, the permittee shall attain compliance with new effluent limits for whole effluent toxicity. The permittee shall conduct a Toxicity Reduction Evaluation (TRE) evaluation as expeditiously as practicable, but not later than the dates in the following schedule."

steps.due_basis: [inference] — the permit says "no later than three months after the effective date"; 2025-07-01 + 3 months.
steps.requirement: Initiate the TRE. The evaluation must include acquisition of plant information (treatment processes, design and operating data, tributary discharges); evaluation of plant and treatment operations as they relate to effluent toxicity, reviewing the adequacy and performance of ALL treatment unit processes; evaluation of in-plant, influent and effluent toxic pollutants to identify the specific toxicants — "including pollutants flowing into the outfalls from off-site"; evaluation of the sources of those toxicants; and evaluation of treatment or source-control measures. "If source toxicity is known, immediate measures shall be taken to control the source."

steps.event_code_note: THE NARRATIVE PRINTS NO EVENT CODE FOR THIS STEP. Items 3 and 4 end "(Event Code 34599)" and "(Event Code 05699)"; item 2 ends at "...other relevant information that has been obtained." with no code. The milestone table's corresponding row (TRE First Monitoring Report, same 2026-04-01 due date) carries `7099` and is transcribed under `milestone_summary_report` above. No zero-padded `07099` appears anywhere in this document — omitted here rather than invented. See event_code_forms below.
steps.requirement: Submit an interim report to the Ohio EPA Northwest District Office detailing the progress of the plant performance evaluation, including any biomonitoring results and other relevant information obtained.

Complete the plant performance evaluation and submit a final report detailing results and conclusions, with recommendations for the actions required to attain compliance with the new WET limits and an implementation schedule with fixed dates. "If necessary, a complete Permit-to-Install (PTI) application and approvable detail plans shall be submitted to Ohio EPA."
Attain compliance with the WET effluent limits, and notify the district office within 14 days of attaining compliance.

toxicity_reduction_evaluation.timing_note: Compliance is due 2028-04-01 but the WET limits do not become enforceable until the 37th month, on or about 2028-07-01 — a three-month margin. The dates are consistent, not contradictory: the schedule requires the plant to be compliant before the limit bites.
toxicity_reduction_evaluation.off_site_clause_note: Step 1(c) reaches "pollutants flowing into the outfalls from off-site", and Part I.C.B below requires local industrial-user limits to be justified. Together they make the TRE a question about the sewershed's industrial users, not only about plant operation. This corpus holds no pretreatment-program records and no industrial-user list, so which users discharge to this POTW is `[open]`.

municipal_pretreatment_schedule.submit_to: "Ohio EPA, Central Office Pretreatment Unit and to Ohio EPA, Northeast District Office" — as printed. See warnings[2]: the TRE schedule names the NORTHWEST district instead.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.requirement: Evaluate the adequacy of local industrial user limitations to prevent pollutants entering the POTW that would interfere with its operation, pass through in amounts exceeding water quality standard-based limits, be incompatible with the POTW, or limit wastewater/sludge use options. Submit either a technical justification for REVISING local limits (with a pretreatment program modification request) or a technical justification for RETAINING the existing ones.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.pollutants_requiring_justification: Arsenic, cadmium, total chromium, dissolved hexavalent chromium, copper, free cyanide, lead, mercury, molybdenum, nickel, selenium, silver and zinc — "unless screening of wastewater and sludge indicate these pollutants are not present in significant amounts" — plus any other pollutant where a local limit may be necessary to protect against pass through, interference or sludge disposal.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.engineering_requirement: If new or revised industrial user discharge limits are proposed, the report requires "the stamp and signature of a licensed Ohio professional engineer."
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.revisions: A revised report is due within 90 days of Ohio EPA notifying the permittee of deficiencies; revised limits must be incorporated into all industrial user control documents no later than 4 months after Ohio EPA's approval.

phosphorus_optimization.event_code_note: The zero-padded form is what THIS section prints ("(Event Code 01299)"). The milestone table prints the same code unpadded as `1299`; both are transcribed where each appears. See event_code_forms below.
phosphorus_optimization.requirement: Prepare and submit for acceptance a Phosphorus Discharge Optimization Evaluation plan — an evaluation of collected effluent data, possible source reduction measures, operational improvements and minor facility modifications that will optimize reductions in phosphorus discharges from the WWTP, including a proposed schedule for implementing any recommended measures.

status_of_these_milestones.lapsed: Three of the five milestone dates are in the past: the pretreatment local-limits justification (2025-10-01), the Phosphorus Optimization Final Plan (2026-04-01) and the TRE First Monitoring Report (2026-04-01). The TRE's own initiation deadline (2025-10-01) has also passed.
status_of_these_milestones.what_is_not_established: WHETHER ANY OF THEM WAS FILED. Nothing in this corpus establishes that — no submittal, no acknowledgment, no violation notice, and no ECHO/ICIS extract for this facility is committed. "Past due" here means the date has passed, NOT that the city missed it. Do not write it as a missed deadline.
status_of_these_milestones.how_to_close_it: A public-records request to Ohio EPA for the 52599, 1299 and 07099 submittals under permit 2PE00001 would settle all three at once, and the TRE interim report in particular would say what the city has found out about the source of its effluent toxicity. Address it to the district office question in warnings[2].

bypass_trigger.text: "The Permittee shall not divert flow through bypass station 2PE00001602 until a sustained peak flow of 19 MGD is being processed through the secondary treatment system. The permittee shall always operate and maintain the equalization basin so as to minimize the discharge through outfall 2PE00001602."
bypass_trigger.significance: A hard numeric precondition on the bypass, and the enforceable form of what the fact sheet describes in volumes. 19 MGD sits between the plant's 12.0 MGD average design flow and the 25 MGD peak recorded in #1429's context. Any bypass event is testable against it: the question "was 19 MGD sustained through secondary first?" is answerable from the plant's own flow record.

biomonitoring_program.text: "The permittee shall CONTINUE TO IMPLEMENT an effluent biomonitoring program to determine the toxicity of the effluent from outfall 2PE00001001."
biomonitoring_program.testing: Chronic and definitive acute toxicity tests for the duration of the permit, on both Ceriodaphnia dubia (water fleas) and Pimephales promelas (fathead minnows), per Ohio EPA's "Reporting and Testing Guidance for Biomonitoring", July 1998 or current revision. The laboratory SOP (or verification of its submittal) was due no later than three months after the effective date — on or about 2025-10-01 [inference].
biomonitoring_program.significance: "Continue to implement" means the biomonitoring program PREDATES this permit. Whatever drove Ohio EPA to write WET limits into the modification was measured under the prior revision (2PE00001*ND), which this corpus does not hold. See warnings[3] on the 001/002 station disagreement.
